table_title: For each continent, list the transboundary rivers included in the cited source set that are longer than 100 miles, including their length in kilometers and the countries they traverse.
db_analog: SELECT continent, river, length_km, countries FROM curated_transboundary_river_source_set WHERE length_miles > 100 ORDER BY continent, river
temporal_note: Wikipedia pages accessed in 2026. Main coverage comes from the Wikipedia "Transboundary river" page section "List of major international transboundary rivers", which is a source-defined list of major rivers rather than an exhaustive list of all qualifying rivers. Fly and Sepik were added from their dedicated pages for Oceania. This staged instance preserves the earlier minimal-supplement source set and should not be interpreted as covering additional omitted rivers later identified during the broader >=1000 km rebuild.
_extraction_notes: Seed draft for the example question. Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and South America rows come from Wikipedia's list of major international transboundary rivers. Oceania rows come from the Fly River and Sepik pages. This staged instance is now framed as a source-defined curated set rather than an exhaustive list of all qualifying rivers. It intentionally preserves the earlier minimal-supplement source set and was not broadened with additional omitted rivers later explored for the >=1000 km sibling instance. River-name normalization follows cited source form where feasible; the Europe/Rhone key was corrected to Europe/Rhône in the CSV.
